claim: Commd1 has stronger affinity than Commd9 for CCDC proteins.
source: Moreover, this assay also suggests that Commd1 has stronger affinity than Commd9 for CCDC proteins.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is an inference from GST pull-down assay data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The affinity (Kd) of the COMM domain of Commd1 with NN-CH of CCDC22 was calculated to be 10.3 µM.
source: A dose-dependent increase in the binding of the COMM domain of Commd1 with NN-CH of CCDC22 and CCDC93 was observed, and the affinity (Kd) was calculated to be 10.3 and 14.6 µM respectively
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by BLiTz data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The affinity (Kd) of the COMM domain of Commd1 with NN-CH of CCDC93 was calculated to be 14.6 µM.
source: A dose-dependent increase in the binding of the COMM domain of Commd1 with NN-CH of CCDC22 and CCDC93 was observed, and the affinity (Kd) was calculated to be 10.3 and 14.6 µM respectively
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by BLiTz data shown in Figure 6C,D.

claim: Cross-linking mass spectrometry identified 5 unique cross-links between Commd9 and NN-CH domain of CCDC93, with 3 pairs connecting the two proteins.
source: Analyses of MS data from band 2 revealed 5 unique cross-links, and 3 of these pairs connected Commd9 and NN-CH domain of CCDC93
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by cross-linking MS data shown in Figure 7B and Table 3.

claim: All three lysines (K100, K133 and K152) identified in cross-linking were located on the surface accessible to the solvent.
source: Mapping of these pairs onto the crystal structures of Commd9 showed that all three lysines (K100, K133 and K152) were located on the surface accessible to the solvent
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by mapping cross-links onto the crystal structure shown in Figure 7C,D.

claim: K133 and K152 are located on contiguous surfaces of the β-sheets of the COMM domains, suggesting a likely binding surface for the CCDC93 NN-CH domain.
source: Notably, K133 and K152 are located on contiguous surfaces of the β-sheets of the COMM domains (Figure 7D), suggesting a likely binding surface for the CCDC93 NN-CH domain.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is an inference based on cross-linking MS data and structural mapping shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The binding surface for CCDC93 includes the side-chains of the conserved residues 128WRVD131, with Trp128 being strictly conserved across the entire Commd family.
source: This surface also includes the side-chains of the conserved residues 128WRVD131, with Trp128 in particular being strictly conserved across the entire Commd family
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is based on structural analysis and sequence conservation data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Commd1 associates relatively non-specifically with various negatively charged membranes.
source: The assay shows that Commd1 associates relatively non-specifically with various negatively charged membranes, including PC/PE liposomes doped with different phosphoinositides, generic Folch lipids from brain extracts, and liposomes containing 30% phosphatidylinositolserine (PS).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by liposome pelleting assay data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Commd7 showed a similar binding characteristic to Commd1 for membrane association.
source: We observed a similar binding characteristic for Commd7
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by liposome pelleting assay data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Commd10 showed a relatively strong interaction with Folch liposomes as well as di- and tri- phosphorylated phosphoinositide species.
source: but Commd10 showed a relatively strong interaction with Folch liposomes as well as di- and tri- phosphorylated phosphoinositide species.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by liposome pelleting assay data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Commd9 appears to associate weakly if at all with the membranes tested.
source: In contrast to the other family members, Commd9 appears to associate weakly if at all with the membranes tested
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by liposome pelleting assay data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: The Commd1 COMM domain exhibits a basic patch on its surface composed of solvent-exposed positively charged residues that are absent in Commd9.
source: A comparative analysis of the electrostatic surface of the COMM domain of Commd9 and a homology model of the COMM domain of Commd1 (constructed using the COMM domain of Commd9 as the template) shows that the Commd1 COMM domain exhibits a basic patch on its surface composed of solvent-exposed positively charged residues that are absent in Commd9
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 8B,C.

claim: The Commd1 triple mutant (R133Q, H134A and K167A) shows a drastic reduction in membrane interaction.
source: To test if this basic surface on Commd1 is involved in membrane recruitment, we made a triple mutant in the putative lipid-binding site (R133Q, H134A and K167A). In liposome-pelleting assays this mutant shows a drastic reduction in membrane interaction
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by liposome pelleting assay data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Commd1 possesses a higher level of binding response for phosphoinositides PI(3)P and PI(4,5)P2 compared to Folch and PS containing membranes.
source: While Commd1 possesses a higher level of binding response for phosphoinositides PI(3)P and PI(4,5)P2 compared to Folch and PS containing membranes
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by BLiTz data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: Commd9 showed little association with any of the lipids tested.
source: Commd9 showed little association with any of the lipids tested, in line with the liposome-pelleting assay
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by BLiTz data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: Commd1 binds to a variety of liposomes with similar affinities in the range of 1–10 µM.
source: Commd1 binds to a variety of liposomes with similar affinities in the range of 1–10 µM, which is in agreement with the qualitative results from pelleting assays
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by BLiTz data shown in Figure 8D,E,F,G and H.

claim: No interaction was observed between liposomes and the Commd1 triple mutant.
source: Confirming the importance of the basic patch on the Commd1 COMM domain, no interaction was observed with the Commd1 triple mutant.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by BLiTz data.

claim: GFP-tagged Commd1 wild type is localized to endosomal puncta and colocalises with the WASH complex subunit Fam21.
source: As seen previously, Commd1 is localized to endosomal puncta, and colocalises with the WASH complex subunit Fam21.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 8I.

claim: The mutant Commd1 (R133Q, H134A, K167A) is also colocalised with Fam21 on endosomes, despite being defective for membrane binding in vitro.
source: Surprisingly however, the mutant Commd1 is also colocalised with Fam21 on endosomes, despite being defective for membrane binding in vitro.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 8I.

claim: The membrane-binding site on Commd1 may be important for non-specific membrane interactions and perhaps for the orientation of the CCC complex on endosomes, but is not required for specific recruitment to PtdIns3P-enriched endosomal compartments in the context of the assembled complex.
source: We propose therefore that this site on Commd1 may instead be important for non-specific membrane interactions and perhaps for the orientation of the CCC complex on endosomes, but in the context of the assembled complex with other COMMD proteins it is not required for specific recruitment to PtdIns3P-enriched endosomal compartments.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and is a speculative interpretation of the immunofluorescence and biochemical data.

claim: The CCC complex is a large endosome-associated assembly that regulates cell surface recycling of various transmembrane receptors.
source: The COMMD proteins were recently identified as conserved and central components of the CCC complex (Mallam and Marcotte, 2017; Wan et al., 2015; McNally et al., 2017), a large endosome-associated assembly that regulates cell surface recycling of various transmembrane receptors
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The solution structures of Commd1, Commd7 and Commd9 reveal a modular architecture with the α-helical N-terminal HN domains arranged as flexible appendages to the C-terminal COMM domain dimers.
source: The solution structures of Commd1, Commd7 and Commd9 reveal a modular architecture with the α-helical N-terminal HN domains arranged as flexible appendages to the C-terminal COMM domain dimers.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and is based on SAXS data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The HN domain is a structurally conserved feature shared by all COMMD family members.
source: Our biophysical, structural and bioinformatics analyses however show that the HN domain is a structurally conserved feature shared by all COMMD family members.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and is based on crystal structures, SAXS data, and bioinformatics analyses presented in the manuscript.

claim: The architecture of the COMMD proteins bears a remarkable resemblance to the orthologous CT584 and Cpn0803, Chlamydia-specific proteins from C. trachomatis and C. pneumonia respectively.
source: The architecture of the COMMD proteins revealed here bears a remarkable resemblance to the orthologous CT584 and Cpn0803, Chlamydia-specific proteins from C. trachomatis and C. pneumonia respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and is based on structural comparison data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Cpn0803 can interact with phospholipids as well as components of the Type III secretion system.
source: The function of these proteins is unknown, although there is evidence that Cpn0803 can interact with phospholipids as well as components of the Type III secretion system responsible for injection of bacterial effectors into the host cytoplasm
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: The CT584/Cpn0803 proteins may be secreted effectors with a potential to mimic or modify COMMD protein functions.
source: We speculate therefore that the CT584/Cpn0803 proteins may be secreted effectors with a potential to mimic or modify COMMD protein functions, although this remains to be confirmed.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and is speculative reasoning based on structural similarity and knowledge of chlamydial biology.

claim: Several chlamydial proteins are believed to have evolved through horizontal gene transfer from eukaryotic hosts.
source: Several chlamydial proteins are believed to have evolved through horizontal gene transfer from eukaryotic hosts, such as SWIB domain-containing proteins and Swi/Snf2 helicases
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations.

claim: It is possible that the CT584/Cpn0803 genes have been acquired through horizontal gene transfer.
source: it is possible that the CT584/Cpn0803 genes have been acquired in a similar fashion
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and is speculative reasoning based on knowledge of horizontal gene transfer in chlamydia.

claim: Both CT584 and Cpn0803 form hexameric structures composed of a trimer of dimers, with the N-terminal domains providing the primary interface for trimer formation.
source: Both CT584 and Cpn0803 form hexameric structures composed of a trimer of dimers, with the N-terminal domains providing the primary interface for trimer formation
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations and reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 4E.

claim: It is tempting to speculate that the N-terminal domains of COMMD proteins will contribute to formation of higher-order heteromeric assemblies that are present in the 600 kDa CCC complexes isolated from cultured cells.
source: While full-length recombinant Commd1, Commd7 and Commd9 proteins analysed here form homodimers, it is tempting to speculate that the N-terminal domains of COMMD proteins will contribute to formation of higher-order heteromeric assemblies that are present in the 600 kDa CCC complexes isolated from cultured cells
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and is speculative reasoning based on structural similarity to chlamydial proteins and knowledge of CCC complex size.

claim: Commd1 was originally identified in dogs with copper toxicosis, which has been mechanistically linked to interactions with the Wilson disease ATPase protein ATP7B.
source: The gene encoding Commd1 (originally called Murr1) was originally identified in dogs with copper toxicosis, which has been mechanistically linked to interactions with the Wilson disease ATPase protein ATP7B
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: Commd1 has been shown to be a potent inhibitor of the transcription factor NF-κB.
source: Most prominently, Commd1 has been shown to be a potent inhibitor of the transcription factor NF-κB, a master regulator of inflammation
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations.

claim: Other COMMD proteins also display similar NF-κB inhibitory activities.
source: Most prominently, Commd1 has been shown to be a potent inhibitor of the transcription factor NF-κB, a master regulator of inflammation, and other COMMD proteins also display similar activities
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations.

claim: Commd1 acts downstream of the inhibitory IκB kinase.
source: Commd1 acts downstream of the inhibitory IκB kinase
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: Commd1 is believed to associate with NF-κB subunits at chromosomal loci and promote NF-κB ubiquitination by Cullin family ubiquitin ligases for degradation.
source: Commd1 acts downstream of the inhibitory IκB kinase (Ganesh et al., 2003), and is believed to associate with NF-κB subunits at chromosomal loci and promote NF-κB ubiquitination by Cullin family ubiquitin ligases for degradation
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations.

claim: A similar function has been proposed for Commd1 regulation of the HIF-1α transcription factor.
source: A similar function has been proposed for Commd1 regulation of the HIF-1α transcription factor
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations.

claim: The COMM domain fold is structurally related to the repeat domains found in the PUR family protein Pur-α.
source: The COMM domain fold is structurally related to the repeat domains found in the PUR (purine-rich element binding protein) family protein Pur-α
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations and structural comparison data.

claim: Pur-α contains three repeat domains, the first two of which form an intramolecular 'dimer' while the third forms an intermolecular dimer that both resemble the dimeric COMM domain topology.
source: Pur-α contains three such repeat domains, the first two of which form an intramolecular 'dimer' while the third forms an intermolecular dimer (Weber et al., 2016) that both resemble the dimeric COMM domain topology.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: Pur-α is a nucleic acid binding protein that plays important roles in the transcription of neuronal genes.
source: Pur-α is a nucleic acid binding protein that plays important roles in the transcription of neuronal genes
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations.

claim: Pur-α is associated with GGGGCC-containing inclusions in ALS-FTD patients.
source: Pur-α is a nucleic acid binding protein that plays important roles in the transcription of neuronal genes (Gallia et al., 2000; White et al., 2009), and is associated with GGGGCC-containing inclusions in ALS-FTD patients
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: The similarity of the COMM domain with Pur-α suggests the intriguing possibility that COMMD proteins could also interact with DNA and/or RNA to regulate transcription.
source: The similarity of the COMM domain with Pur-α suggests the intriguing possibility that COMMD proteins could also interact with DNA and/or RNA to regulate transcription
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and is speculative reasoning based on structural similarity.

claim: The specific DNA binding site in Pur-α is not conserved in the COMMD proteins.
source: although it should be noted that the specific DNA binding site in Pur-α (Weber et al., 2016) is not conserved in the COMMD proteins
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and is based on structural comparison shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3A.

claim: The CCC complex and associated COMMD proteins are predominantly localised to early endosomal membranes.
source: The CCC complex and associated COMMD proteins are predominantly localised to early endosomal membranes
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations.

claim: COMMD proteins show significant but non-preferential binding to a variety of negatively charged lipids.
source: COMMD proteins show significant but non-preferential binding to a variety of negatively charged lipids, and these interactions appear to be maintained by the COMM domain.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and is based on liposome pelleting and BLiTz data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The HN domain is dispensable for membrane association.
source: Our data also highlights that the HN domain is dispensable for membrane association, which is in line with the work of Burkhead et al.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and is based on experimental data and supported by a citation.

claim: The membrane-binding surface of Commd1 in vitro is composed of residues from both molecules of the homodimer.
source: The membrane-binding surface of Commd1 in vitro is composed of residues from both molecules of the homodimer
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and is based on structural analysis and mutagenesis data.

claim: The membrane-binding surface of Commd1 does not appear essential for endosomal localisation of Commd1 in cells.
source: but interestingly this does not appear essential for endosomal localisation of Commd1 in cells
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and is based on immunofluorescence data showing mutant Commd1 still localizes to endosomes.

claim: The ability of COMMD proteins to associate with membranes is only one part of a more complicated array of interactions controlling specific endosomal membrane recruitment.
source: This suggests that the ability of COMMD proteins to associate with membranes is only one part of a more complicated array of interactions controlling specific endosomal membrane recruitment
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and is an inference based on the observation that membrane-binding mutants still localize to endosomes.

claim: The depletion of CCDC93 or the WASH complex subunit Fam21 both lead to a loss of Commd1 from endosomes.
source: Supporting a role for other subunits and complexes in specific endosomal localisation of the CCC complex, the depletion of CCDC93 or the WASH complex subunit Fam21 both lead to a loss of Commd1 from endosomes
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: The depletion of CCDC22 causes a redistribution of Commd1 and Commd10.
source: while the depletion of CCDC22 causes a redistribution of Commd1 and Commd10
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: The ability to self-assemble and form heteromeric complexes is a core property of the COMMD proteins.
source: The ability to self-assemble and form heteromeric complexes is a core property of the COMMD proteins identified in some of the very first studies
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: Coordinates and structure factors for the COMM and HN domain of Commd9 have been deposited at the Protein Data Bank (PDB) with accession codes 6BP6 (COMM domain Commd9) and 4OE9 (HN domain of Commd9).
source: Coordinates and structure factors for the COMM and HN domain of Commd9 have been deposited at the Protein Data Bank (PDB) with accession codes 6BP6 (COMM domain Commd9) and 4OE9 (HN domain of Commd9).
evidence: This is stated in the Data availability section and represents the deposition of structural data.
